## Overview

LRPITT15 compares two available-case modified ITT estimates to test whether the assigned-arm contrast is larger for directly-taught than not-taught expressive vocabulary, one component of the trial's broader generalisation claim. Two Block 1 expressive vocabulary outcomes are fitted together as factorised marginals over the randomised window (t1 $\rightarrow$ t2):

- `TE` — directly-taught target words (`b1extau`, $N = 24$);
- `UE` — not-taught comparison words (`b1exnt`, $N = 12$).

The headline quantity is the difference between the two standardised probability-scale average marginal effects, $\mathrm{AME}_{\mathrm{TE}} - \mathrm{AME}_{\mathrm{UE}}$. A positive value means the model estimates a larger assigned-arm difference in expected proportion correct for taught expressive words than for not-taught expressive words. It does **not** by itself show that generalisation was limited: that conclusion also requires the marginal UE contrast to be small against a substantively defined negligible-effect threshold. The conditional logit-coefficient difference is secondary. The receptive companion is LRPITT15b; the per-outcome models are LRPITT02 (TE) and LRPITT04 (UE).

Randomisation created exchangeability in the original full randomised cohort, so these offer contrasts require no baseline-covariate adjustment there. The fitted factorised contrast instead conditions on archive inclusion and the required observed variables for both outcomes. A causal reading of either component or their difference requires that this selection did not induce an association between assigned arm and the potential values of either outcome; extending the result to all 57 randomised children requires further missing-data assumptions and sensitivity.

## Structure

For child $i$ and outcome $k \in \{\mathrm{TE}, \mathrm{UE}\}$:

$$
\eta_{k,i} = \alpha_k + \tau_k G_i
           + \gamma^{\text{own}}_k\, \text{logit}_*(k_{\text{pre},i}, N_k)
           + \gamma^{A}_k\, A_{\text{std},i},
$$

with a per-outcome Beta-Binomial likelihood and dispersion $\kappa_k$. The 2×2 LKJ residual-correlation block is **off**, so the likelihood and priors factorise by outcome. This avoids the poor mixing seen in an earlier sensitivity fit but does not estimate within-child posterior covariance. Ignoring that covariance is not guaranteed to be conservative: the direction depends on the unknown sign and magnitude. The current contrast is therefore an exploratory factorised sensitivity result, not calibrated paired inference; confirmation requires a dependence-model analysis — the registered companion `lrp-rli-itt-215` (#551) — or a paired child-level randomisation-inference/permutation, bootstrap or sandwich analysis.

_Denominators and caveats._

- Taught ($\mathrm{TE}$): $N = 24$ — documented (Burgoyne et al., 2012, Table 3).
- Not-taught ($\mathrm{UE}$): $N = 12$ — confirmed (#214; `n_trials_confirmed=True` in `measures.py`).
- The headline contrast is a difference in expected proportion correct, so it is not distorted merely because one test has 24 items and the other 12. Instrument content, difficulty and measurement precision remain different.
- A positive taught-minus-not-taught difference establishes only that the taught effect is larger. Assess whether transfer is small from the marginal UE AME against a substantively defined negligible-effect threshold.
- $n \approx 54$; this is an archived observed-data contrast over the randomised window, with the selection and missing-data qualifications above.
- The factorised fit does not estimate within-child residual covariance. The registered dependence-model sensitivity is [`lrp-rli-itt-215`](../lrp-rli-itt-215) (#551): the same contrast with `use_residual_correlation=True`, published as a posterior difference that carries the estimated within-child covariance. Read its interval and P(> 0) beside this one — the companion adds a per-child logistic-normal offset, so its point estimate is a different (latent-conditional) estimand and is not invariant by construction, although the two agree closely here — and treat this contrast as dependence-checked only once that companion has passed the house gate; until then the report must not make a definitive paired generalisation claim.
- PSIS-LOO leaves out a child by summing that child's observed outcome-cell log likelihoods.
